summary: Walter Ruben was an Indologist. He held academic posts at Goethe University Frankfurt (~1931–1935), the University of Chile (~1948–1949), and the University of Berlin (~1950–1965).

Walter Simon specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics. Educated at the University of Berlin under Otto Franke and August Hermann Francke, he served at the University of Berlin, the National Library of China, and the University of London.

Walter Slaje is an Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna. He worked at Graz University Library (1984–1995) and served as Director at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from 1995 to 2020.

Walter William Skeat worked in linguistics. He studied at King's College School, Highgate School, and Christ's College, Cambridge (~1854–1858), and later held a post at the University of Cambridge from ~1878 to 1912.

Walter Yeeling Evans-Wentz worked in religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Stanford University (~1902–1907), the University of Oxford and Jesus College, Oxford (1907–1911), and under Kazi Dawa Samdup (~1919–1922).

Walther Heissig worked in Central Asian studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Berlin, Vienna, Göttingen, and Bonn, and held posts at Peking University, Fu Jen Catholic University (~1941–1945), and the University of Bonn (1964).

Walther Schubring was an Indologist who studied at the University of Munich and under Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg (~1902–1904). He worked at the Prussian State Library (1907) and held the Indology chair at Hamburg (1920–1951).

Walther Wüst worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Munich (1920–1923), where he served as Dean of the Faculty of Philosophy (1935–1945), and headed a division at Ahnenerbe (1936).
Wang Pachow was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied under Tan Yun-shan and served on the teaching and research staff at Visva-Bharati University.

Wannaporn Rienjang specializes in archaeology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Cambridge, worked at the British Museum and the University of Oxford (attested 2019–2022), and lectures at Thammasat University (attested 2022–2023).
Warren Cowgill was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Stanford University (~1948–1952) and Yale University (~1952–1957), where he became a professor of linguistics in 1956.

Warren Lee Todd is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He earned his PhD at Lancaster University, studying under doctoral supervisor Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad (attested 2012), Irina Kuznetsova, Peter Harvey, and Chogye Trichen Rinpoche.

Warrin Ratanamalai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Suthithammanuwat and Phra Srisitthimuni, having also studied under Phra Sudhivorayan and Phramaha Somjin Sammāpañño.
Watari Yanai was a scholar in Sinology, history and archaeology, and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1900 to 1903 and later held a post there from ~1919 to 1926.

Wataru Mori worked in philosophy and other fields. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1951) and later held posts at Tokyo Medical and Dental University (~1968–1973) and the University of Tokyo (~1973–1989).

Wataru S. Ryose is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin–Madison in 1987 under Minoru Kiyota, having also studied under Genjun Sasaki and Frances A. Wilson.

Wayne Proudfoot is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Harvard Divinity School and Harvard University (~1966–1972) and taught at Fordham University before serving as Professor of Religion at Columbia University (~1972–2008).

Wei Lin specializes in archaeology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Nanjing, Peking, and Ohio State (PhD under John C. Huntington), Lin held posts at Nanjing Municipal Museum, Western Michigan, Michigan, Ohio State, and Transylvania University (attested 2007).

Wei-jen Teng works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. Teng studied at the University of Chicago and earned a PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, later teaching at Dharma Drum Institute.

Weijue Shi was a Buddhist studies and religious figure. He studied under Lingshuan and was ordained under Lingyuan (~1963). He founded Lin Quan Temple in 1987, the Chung Tai Buddhist Institute in 1993, and Chung Tai Shan.
